response: {"title":"Three-layer verification cap","intervention":"Allocate verification time in order to import and syntax checks, tests for changed modules, and one cross-module smoke path, giving each layer at most one third of the verification budget and immediately advancing when a layer passes.","claim":"Against no appended instruction, this three-layer cap will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses for multi-module Python coding tasks run under equal deadlines.","mechanism":"Cheap universal failures are detected first, local behavioral regressions second, and integration breakage third, while per-layer caps prevent any single test class from exhausting the deadline.","assumptions":["The agent can estimate or infer a verification budget from the deadline.","Changed-module tests and a representative cross-module smoke path exist or can be run cheaply.","The three failure classes cover a meaningful share of benchmark failures."],"risks":["Equal thirds may be poorly matched to task-specific risk.","A hanging or slow command can exceed its intended cap without reliable timeout support.","One smoke path may not represent important integrations.","Time spent on import checks may be redundant when the test runner performs them."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly apply the appended instruction to half of a matched set of fixed-deadline multi-module Python tasks, using no appended instruction for controls and identical models, tools, and scoring.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment pass_rate exceeds control and treatment deadline-miss frequency does not exceed control; compare wall_time and turns to expose added effort."},"single_shot_ordinal":4}
